incentive_fee_definition.authority: Note 3 — Agreements and Related Party Transactions, Q2-2026 10-Q (accession 0001655888-26-000056), plus Part I Item 1 'Investment Advisory Agreement' of the FY2025 10-K (0001655888-26-000010).
incentive_fee_definition.income_component_verbatim: 'The portion of the incentive fee based on pre-incentive fee net investment income is determined and paid quarterly in arrears for the immediately preceding calendar quarter commencing with the first calendar quarter following July 18, 2019 (the “Listing Date”), and equals 100% of the pre-incentive fee net investment income in excess of a 1.5% quarterly “hurdle rate,” until the Adviser has received 17.5% of the total pre-incentive fee net investment income for that calendar quarter and, for pre-incentive fee net investment income in excess of 1.82% quarterly, 17.5% of all remaining pre-incentive fee net investment income for that calendar quarter.'
incentive_fee_definition.definition_verbatim: Pre-incentive fee net investment income means dividends (including reinvested dividends), interest and fee income accrued by us during the calendar quarter, minus operating expenses for the calendar quarter (including the management fee, expenses payable under the Administration Agreement, and any interest expense and dividends paid on any issued and outstanding preferred stock, but excluding the incentive fee). Pre-incentive fee net investment income includes, in the case of investments with a deferred interest feature (such as original issue discount, debt instruments with pay-in-kind interest (“PIK”) and zero coupon securities), accrued income that we may not have received in cash. The Adviser is not obligated to return the incentive fee it receives on PIK interest that is later determined to be uncollectible in cash. Pre-incentive fee net investment income does not include any realized capital gains, realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation. [OBDC adds:] '...or any amortization or accretion of any purchase premium or purchase discount to interest income resulting solely from the purchase accounting for any premium or discount paid for the acquisition of assets in a merger.'
incentive_fee_definition.does_pre_incentive_fee_nii_INCLUDE_accru: YES — explicitly, in the same words as OTF.
incentive_fee_definition.pik_language_verbatim: 'Pre-incentive fee net investment income includes, in the case of investments with a deferred interest feature (such as original issue discount, debt instruments with pay-in-kind interest (“PIK”) and zero coupon securities), accrued income that we may not have received in cash. The Adviser is not obligated to return the incentive fee it receives on PIK interest that is later determined to be uncollectible in cash.'
incentive_fee_definition.does_the_income_hurdle_or_cap_NET_OUT_un: NO. 'Pre-incentive fee net investment income does not include any realized capital gains, realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation...'
incentive_fee_definition.total_return_lookback: ABSENT — identical to OTF. No total-return hurdle, no lookback, nothing to bind.
incentive_fee_definition.capital_gains_component_verbatim: '...equals 17.5% of cumulative realized capital gains from the Listing Date to the end of each calendar year, less cumulative realized capital losses and unrealized capital depreciation from the Listing Date to the end of each calendar year, less the aggregate amount of any previously paid capital gains incentive fee for prior periods provided, however, that the calculation ... shall not include any realized capital gains, realized capital losses or unrealized capital appreciation or depreciation resulting solely from the purchase accounting for any premium or discount paid for the acquisition of assets in a merger.'
incentive_fee_definition.management_fee_verbatim: 'The management fee is payable at an annual rate of (x) 1.50% of the Company's average gross assets ... that is above an asset coverage ratio of 200% ... and (y) 1.00% ... that is below an asset coverage ratio of 200%.'

fees_actually_charged.source: Note 3 tables; Statements of Operations line 'Performance based incentive fees'.

incentive_fee_definition.mechanism_finding: SAME MECHANISM, LARGER DOLLARS. OBDC charged $68.6m of income incentive fee for 1H-2026 while NAV fell $14.81 -> $14.26 and net unrealized depreciation ran -$196.3m with realized losses of -$97.6m. Unlike OTF, OBDC took NO capital-gains-fee reversal offset ($0 in both periods) because cumulative realized losses since the 2019 Listing Date already exceed gains — so the accrual is already at zero and cannot go further negative to cushion shareholders. Marginal fee on the $89.2m of 1H PIK at 17.5% is ~$15.6m (~$7.5m in Q2, ~21% of the Q2 fee) — SignalOS estimate, not a filed number.
incentive_fee_definition.differs_from_OTF_detail: The two post-listing templates are IDENTICAL: same 17.5% rate, same 1.5% quarterly hurdle, same 100% catch-up to 1.82%, same capital-gains formula netting unrealized depreciation, same 1.50%/1.00% management fee split at 200% asset coverage, and a word-for-word identical pre-incentive-fee NII definition including the PIK inclusion and the explicit no-clawback sentence. Only difference: OBDC carves out merger purchase-accounting premium/discount accretion (a consequence of the OBDE merger), which REDUCES the fee base rather than inflating it. Adviser incentive is held constant across the pair.

control_strata_fv_over_cost.psec_benchmark: PSEC control book 111.1% of cost vs arm's-length 90.2% — a 20.9-point gap on 58% of the portfolio.
control_strata_fv_over_cost.finding: THE PSEC PATTERN IS PRESENT, AT HALF THE AMPLITUDE AND A QUARTER THE SIZE. OBDC's arm's-length book marks at 97.24% of cost; its CONTROLLED book — self-originated, self-valued, no third-party trade reference — marks at 111.40%. That is a 14.2-point gap (PSEC's was 20.9) on 14.1% of portfolio cost (PSEC's was 58%). Controlled affiliates are also the ONLY strata with positive unrealized in Q2 (+$20.4m against -$110.0m arm's-length) and supply $44.7m of dividend income in Q2 = 11.1% of total investment income. Largest marks: Wingspire Capital Holdings $607.1m at 120.3% of cost (8.6% of NAV); Eagle Infrastructure Services common units $101.7m at 422.6% of cost; New PLI Holdings Class A units $87.9m at 183.1%; AAM Series 2.1 equity at 149.4%; Fifth Season at 114.2%. Offsetting honesty: the Blue Owl Credit SLF JV is marked DOWN to 90.2% of cost and PS Op Holdings equity to zero.
control_strata_fv_over_cost.classification_caveat: NOT directly comparable to OTF's strata. Fifth Season, LSI Financing LLC and both AAM feeders are CONTROLLED for OBDC but NON-CONTROLLED AFFILIATED for OTF, purely because OBDC owns more. Compare the affiliated-combined line: OBDC 108.41% of cost on 15.4% of portfolio cost vs OTF 103.11% on 6.7%.

structural_notes.merger_overhang: OBDE was merged into OBDC on 1/13/2025 and accounted for as an asset acquisition with a purchase discount. The discount amortizes into interest income with an offsetting unrealized depreciation — $5.6m in Q2-2026, $11.8m in 1H — so GAAP NII is flattered and GAAP unrealized is penalised by an equal amount. OBDC discloses this and publishes a non-GAAP 'adjusted' series; the incentive fee explicitly excludes it. Disclosed, not hidden.

coverage_gaps: The Q1-2026 10-Q gives the non-accrual cost/FV table but no count of portfolio companies on non-accrual, so the 2026Q1 count is not reported.
LSI Financing LLC discloses no unit/share count — only a commitment/par figure — so the cross-vehicle mark comparison versus OTF can only be tested on FV/par.
Fifth Season Investments LLC unit counts are whole integers (27 for OBDC, 12 for OTF), limiting per-unit cross-vehicle resolution to about +/-4%.

Wingspire Capital Holdings, Eagle Infrastructure Services and the PLI/Beauty Industry Group entities are wholly adviser-valued with no cross-vehicle mirror position at OTF, so the same-adviser consistency test cannot reach them at all. This is where the mark risk is least testable.
Quarterly NII per share and quarterly PIK for Q4-2025 are DERIVED by differencing cumulative filed figures.
Estimated incentive fee attributable to PIK (~$7.5m in Q2-2026) is a SignalOS marginal-rate computation, not a disclosed figure.
Tax characterization of 2026 distributions is not determined until year end.
Liquidation preferences on PIK preferred equity are not disclosed, invalidating the per-share cross-vehicle test on PIK-accreting preferreds.
